newsitem.title: FINLAND: West's visa policy creates iron curtain - Moscow.
newsitem.headline: West's visa policy creates iron curtain - Moscow.

text.p: A Russian official accused the United States and other Western countries on Thursday of erecting a new "iron curtain" by operating tough visa policies against Russians.

Mikhail Timoshkin, a senior foreign ministry official dealing with immigration and consular matters, said at the Helsinki summit that Moscow has liberated its visa policies since communist rule ended but Western countries had not always responded in similar fashion.

"As President (Ronald) Reagan once said, it takes two to tango. We are ready to tango but our Western partners unfortunately were not ready for the flow of Russian citizens," Timoshkin told a news conference.

"You journalists often talked about the iron curtain around Russia. Now we detect that iron curtain on the part of Western countries which for various reasons try everything they can to complicate procedures for receiving Russian citizens."
Timoshkin, speaking before presidents Bill Clinton and Boris Yeltsin began the Russia-U.S. summit, singled out the United States for criticism.
He said about one in every four Russians applying for visas to visit the United States were refused. "We do not think this is an acceptable norm for countries with partnerly relations," he said.
Timoshkin said Moscow reserved the right to take "adequate measures" against countries which Moscow considered were discriminating against Russians but gave no details.
Some countries fear that Russian criminal gangs, which have flourished since communist rule ended in 1991, could take a hold abroad.
